prompt: Camila said she was leaving for more pay and a shorter commute. What did her one-to-one notes show?

choices.text: Nothing beyond what she said
choices.why: Rereading the notes found three earlier causes.

choices.text: Requests for front-end work put off twice, a growth section empty since the autumn, and two holidays on call in a row
choices.why: Right: all visible for months, and none would appear in an exit survey.

choices.text: A conflict with Diego
choices.why: Nothing like that is in her notes.

choices.text: That she had been on an improvement plan earlier in the year, which nobody had mentioned to Renata
choices.why: She was steady and well liked; there was no plan.

prompt: Match each reason for leaving with who has most control over it, by the lesson’s table.

pairs.right: the company, with the manager’s advocacy

prompt: In Herzberg’s terms, which of these is a motivator rather than a hygiene factor?
hint: Bad hygiene dissatisfies; good hygiene motivates little.

choices.text: Salary
choices.why: A hygiene factor: its absence dissatisfies, its presence motivates little.

choices.text: Company policies on working hours, leave and expenses
choices.why: Policies are hygiene factors.

choices.text: Office conditions
choices.why: Conditions are a hygiene factor.

choices.text: Recognition for work done
choices.why: Right: achievement, recognition, responsibility and growth are what motivate.

prompt: Renata could not have matched Camila’s new salary. What does the lesson say was within her reach?

choices.text: A counter-offer
choices.why: Caju made none, because her reasons were not mainly money.

choices.text: A real answer on front-end work, noticing the empty growth section, and asking about leaving earlier
choices.why: Right: each was a reason within her control, visible months before the resignation.

choices.text: Nothing: a better offer is outside a manager’s control
choices.why: The offer was, the earlier reasons were not.

choices.text: A promotion to senior, which would have come with a salary close to the other company’s
choices.why: Promotion follows evidence on the ladder, not retention.

prompt: A team of 20, on average over the year, lost 3 people. What is its attrition rate, as a percentage?
Agenda averaged 7 people over the year and lost 2, one of them regretted. What was the regretted attrition rate, to one decimal place?
Why does the lesson say a rate for a team of seven says little on its own?

choices.text: Small teams have no attrition
choices.why: Agenda lost two people.

choices.text: Single events
choices.why: Right: almost 29% was two people.

choices.text: Because only the company-wide rate is calculated correctly, with the average headcount
choices.why: Any team’s rate can be calculated correctly; small teams are just noisy.

choices.text: Seven is below the legal minimum for reporting
choices.why: No legal minimum is mentioned.

prompt: Which line does the lesson say is always the question for a manager?

choices.text: Regretted departures
choices.why: Right: losing the people the team most needs matters whatever the total says.

choices.text: The total attrition rate, since it is what the company compares across teams
choices.why: The total hides whether the people lost were the ones the team wanted.

choices.text: Involuntary departures
choices.why: A different split, and not the one the lesson singles out.

choices.text: Unregretted departures
choices.why: These may mean performance is handled honestly.

prompt: What makes a stay conversation more useful than an exit interview?

choices.text: It is anonymous
choices.why: It is a one-to-one, not anonymous.

choices.text: It is shorter
choices.why: Length is not the point.

choices.text: It comes while the person has not decided, and their answer still has a chance to change something
choices.why: Right: an exit interview asks when nothing can change and the person has every reason to be polite.

choices.text: Because HR runs it, so people are more honest than they would be with their own manager
choices.why: The manager runs it, in a one-to-one.

prompt: Why is “When was the last time you thought about leaving?” the most useful of the five questions?

choices.text: It catches people who are about to resign
choices.why: It is not a trap; it surfaces causes.

choices.text: It treats thinking about leaving as normal and asks for a specific moment
choices.why: Right: a specific moment points at a specific cause.

choices.text: Because people answer it with a yes or no, which makes it easy to compare across the team
choices.why: It asks for a moment, not yes or no.

choices.text: Because it is the hardest to answer
choices.why: People hesitate over it, but that is not why it is useful.

prompt: Which of these did people on Agenda name as moments they had thought about leaving? Choose all that apply.

choices.text: Yara: the risk of being pulled back to work on Agenda alone
choices.why: Yes: what would make her leave.

choices.text: Lucas: the onboarding
choices.why: No: the question had never occurred to him.

choices.text: Thiago: on-call
choices.why: No: Thiago said he had not thought about it.

choices.text: Diego: a staff case refused without explanation
choices.why: Yes, under the previous manager.

choices.text: Paula: the year nobody noticed her glue work
choices.why: Yes.

prompt: Money offered to stay after a resignation is called a ___-offer.

A strong engineer resigns citing salary. The manager wants to counter-offer. The engineer’s notes show two years without new work and repeated, unanswered requests to change teams. What does this lesson suggest?
hint: After the raise, what is still there?

choices.text: Counter-offer at once, since salary was the reason she gave in the exit conversation
choices.why: The reason given is the safest one; the notes show others.

choices.text: The real reasons stay after a raise
choices.why: Right: growth and the unanswered requests remain after a raise.

choices.text: Promote her to keep her
choices.why: Promotion follows the ladder, and does not fix the lack of new work.

choices.text: Ask her colleagues why she is leaving
choices.why: Her own notes already say much of it.
